intro: I know you’re going through a lot of applications, so I’ve put together some highlights on how I align with what you’re looking for.

I've been building content systems for a long time. My first one was a homemade PHP CMS in 2000 for a webcomic and forum. Later I led a publisher's move from a custom CMS to WordPress. A CMS that serves marketers and agents at the same time is the most interesting version of that problem I've seen.

requirements.heading: Making complex content infrastructure feel obvious
requirements.body: At WorkStep, I led a product-wide IA re-architecture with our Senior PM. This project touched navigation, information hierarchy, and dozens of existing features at once. Multi-phase, cross-team, and I owned the direction the whole way through. A CMS with content models, locales, sites, and publishing states is a similar exercise.

images.alt: Information architecture work from the WorkStep IA re-architecture

requirements.heading: Content and publishing tools, from the inside
requirements.body: At The Daily Dot I led UX for our internal publishing tools and the migration from a custom CMS to WordPress. Editors were moving fast on deadline, so every extra step in authoring or publishing showed up immediately. At Foxtrot I ran content audits and IA for clients like Dimensional Fund Advisors and the Austin Film Society. I've seen what happens to content when the model underneath it is wrong.

images.alt: Plain-language helper text in a WorkStep segment builder

requirements.heading: Designing for humans and agents
requirements.body: At WorkStep I designed an LLM-powered assistant with our data scientist and CPO that turned workforce data into plain-language insights for managers. I also designed LLM-based grouping that made thousands of open-ended survey comments readable. On my own time I'm building a landscaping app in Figma through the Figma MCP, so I spend a lot of hours watching an agent work against a structured system. Good structure is what makes agents reliable, and clear controls are what make people trust them.

images.alt: Some of the various mobile and web designs I've done

requirements.heading: Systems that survive translation
requirements.body: Localization breaks layouts in predictable ways: German runs long, Japanese changes line height, and right-to-left flips everything. I design components to hold up across languages and still pass contrast checks, and I check them in more than one language before calling them done.

images.alt: A button translated into a dozen languages, with a contrast checker

requirements.heading: Design systems with judgment
requirements.body: I rebuilt WorkStep's Figma design system from scratch on variables and tokens, with aliasing so a change at the token level ripples everywhere. Component bloat dropped by 85%, and everything is built to WCAG AA contrast. I've also learned well what does and doesn't belong in a design system, which is half the job.

images.alt: Example design system from a project with Halliburton

requirements.heading: Comfortable where design meets production
requirements.body: I've been writing HTML and CSS since 1999, and I maintain my own site in Vue. I prototype in code with Claude Code every day, so talking through content models, API shapes, and data structures with engineers feels normal to me. This page was published by a workflow I built that turns a job posting into structured JSON and renders it through a dynamic route on my site. That's a tiny headless CMS, and building it taught me a lot.

requirements.heading: Presenting tradeoffs without losing the room
requirements.body: As Head of Design at Unilease and a lead at T3 and Foxtrot, I presented to CEOs and Fortune 500 stakeholders and mentored other designers. I like making the reasoning visible so partners can disagree with it productively, and I'd rather test an assumption early than defend it late.

requirements.heading: Where I'd be learning
requirements.body: I haven't designed a commercial CMS for enterprise marketing teams, and localization workflows at Webflow's scale would be new to me. I've been a Webflow-adjacent builder for years from the outside, hand-coding sites that marketers then had to live with. I'd want to spend early time with your customers and your agentic platform engineers to learn where content actually gets stuck.
